record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.context_brief: Finite Ramsey principles and weak pigeonhole
record.original_question: For the finite Ramsey-type principles FRT^e_k(Σ_{n+1}), determine whether IΣ_{n+1} + WPHP(Σ_{n+1}) proves FRT^2_2(Σ_{n+1}), and whether FRT^2_2(Σ_{n+1}) implies FRT^2_3(Σ_{n+1}).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the language of first-order arithmetic. For each n ≥ 0, let Σ_{n+1} denote the class of Σ_{n+1} formulas in this language, and let IΣ_{n+1} be the fragment of Peano arithmetic consisting of the basic axioms together with the induction scheme restricted to Σ_{n+1} formulas. The weak pigeonhole principle WPHP(Σ_{n+1}) is the scheme stating that for every Σ_{n+1}-definable (with parameters) function f and every x > 0, there is no map f : {0,1,…,2x} → {0,1,…,x−1} with all values below x; equivalently, no Σ_{n+1}-definable function maps {0,…,2x} injectively into {0,…,x−1}.

For natural numbers e, k ≥ 2 the finite Ramsey-type principle FRT^e_k(Σ_{n+1}) is the following scheme: for every Σ_{n+1}-definable coloring c : [N]^e → {0,1,…,k−1} of the e-element subsets of {0,1,…,N−1} in k colors (with parameters), and for every m, there exists N large enough that some homogeneous subset of {0,…,N−1} of size at least m exists, i.e. a set H ⊆ {0,…,N−1} with |H| ≥ m on which c is constant.

Determine whether each of the following holds:
(a) IΣ_{n+1} + WPHP(Σ_{n+1}) ⊢ FRT^2_2(Σ_{n+1}).
(b) Over IΣ_{n+1}, FRT^2_2(Σ_{n+1}) ⊢ FRT^2_3(Σ_{n+1}).
artifact.category_tag: Fragments of arithmetic and Ramsey principles
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a recent list of open problems in computability theory and descriptive set theory, and a web search returned no published solution addressing these specific implications between FRT^2_2(Σ_{n+1}), FRT^2_3(Σ_{n+1}), and IΣ_{n+1} + WPHP(Σ_{n+1}).

status_evidence.title: On the 'finitary' Ramsey's theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses FRT-style principles and their provability strength over fragments of arithmetic, without resolving the stated implications.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on finitary Ramsey principles in fragments of arithmetic, but does not settle the two implications in question.

status_evidence.title: The Paris–Harrington principle and second-order arithmetic
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys Paris–Harrington-type principles and their relationship to IΣ_n hierarchy.
status_evidence.claim: Provides context for FRT-type principles but does not address WPHP(Σ_{n+1}) ⊢ FRT^2_2(Σ_{n+1}) or FRT^2_2 ⊢ FRT^2_3.
